verdict: OK to lend in Ballari iron & steel — pursue re-rollers and service units tied to the JSW and Uttama Galva build-out, structure tightly around iron-ore and power cost swings, and avoid pure ore-trading and single-customer units.
title: Ballari iron & steel: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Ballari steel is ore-to-billet-to-roll: sponge iron and re-rolling units buy iron ore and coal, melt and roll, and sell TMT and structurals into Karnataka and neighbouring states.** Cash is made on the spread between ore-plus-power cost and finished-steel price, not on volume alone. The working-capital cycle is short on the sales side but heavy on inventory — ore and coal stock plus power security deposits sit ahead of the cash. Capex is lumpy: a re-rolling line or captive power unit is a multi-year commitment. **So when a proposal lands, check the ore and power cost per tonne against the selling price per tonne; if the spread is thin, ask what protects it.**

## What has changed now
**The district is on the edge of a large capacity build-out: Uttama Galva Ferrous has environment clearance for a 60 lakh tonne per year steel plant with an 893 MW captive power plant [1], and JSW Steel has placed a mega expansion order for Ballari [3].** Peer results confirm the demand side is real — JSW Steel's September-quarter profit more than tripled on better volumes and higher prices [4], and Kirloskar Ferrous posted record volumes but saw margins eroded by coking coal and rupee depreciation [6]. **The margin story is the warning: volume growth is not margin growth, so when a proposal lands, check the input-cost pass-through clause; if there is none, ask for the last four quarters' cost-to-price movement.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue the second-tier suppliers and service units that will feed these plants — fabrication, handling, transport, and small re-rollers with an offtake link to JSW or Uttama Galva.** Karnataka's local demand signals support this: GST collections are up 11.1% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and electricity demand is up 23.3% against India's 9.5% [D]. **Avoid pure iron-ore traders and units with a single customer or a single furnace; the mining regulatory risk is live — the Supreme Court-appointed committee has been urged to visit Ballari's mining-hit areas [2].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the input cycle, not the order book: keep tenor short, take a charge on stock and receivables, and set a covenant on the ore-plus-power cost per tonne.** Take monthly stock statements and monthly power bills — power is the second-largest cost and the earliest signal of a utilisation drop.
